title: The King's Indian chain and its pawn breaks

D0.outcome: States the app's working definition (pawns on c4, d5 and e4 against pawns on d6, e5 and g6; colours may be reversed) and the main idea: the centre is locked, so each side attacks on its own wing and the two plans are a race.

D1.outcome: Told the structure, names each side's pawn break and target: Black's ...f5 against e4 and the kingside pawn advance, White's c4-c5 against the d6 base, and which wing each plan uses.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions decides whether to start the break now, prepare it, or stop the opponent's break, by comparing the speed of the two attacks.

D3.outcome: Predicts how one-feature changes (the f-pawn already on f3, a knight on e8 or f6, the c-file closed or opened) change the race, and checks the verdict with the engine.

misconceptions: The king's-side pawn storm always works because the centre is locked.
The side with the slower break can ignore the other wing.
The bishop on g7 is a good piece because it is fianchettoed.

rating.note: expert estimate; tier=5; definition and plans are ours; the chain-base idea is Nimzowitsch's

conditions: Working definition (new, the app's own, not claimed to match any book): one side has pawns on c4, d5 and e4, the other has pawns on d6, e5 and g6; the colours may be reversed.
Attack the base of the chain, not its head: the c4-c5 break hits d6, the base of the chain d6-e5, and the two sides play on opposite wings.
Each side's attack is a race on its own wing: the side whose break arrives first with its pieces behind it usually decides, and the slower side must stop the other's break before hurrying its own.
The pawns d6 and e5 stand on the colour of the g7 bishop, so that bishop is limited until a break or a trade opens its diagonal.
condition_sources: ours; not yet implemented in gen_struct.py
contrasts: The kingside break is played before the pieces and the king are ready: it loses time or weakens e5 and g6.
The queenside break c4-c5 is played when the opponent's kingside attack is already faster: the break is a move too slow.
The d-pawns have been exchanged, so no chain exists (a Benoni or open-centre position): the plans above do not apply.

soft_prereq_notes.POS.GOODBAD.D2: the g7 bishop behind its own pawns is a good-bishop-or-bad-bishop question
soft_prereq_notes.DEF.SHELTER.D1: pawn advances toward the king loosen its cover on both sides
